title: Saba sends gifts to Assyria
description: An Assyrian inscription records gifts of precious stones and perfumes from Karib'il, ruler of Saba, to King Sennacherib, an early dated reference to the kingdom that grew rich on the incense trade.

title: Roman expedition reaches Marib
description: An army under Aelius Gallus, prefect of Egypt, marches into southern Arabia on the orders of Augustus and turns back after failing to take Marib.

title: Himyar conquers Saba
description: The Himyarite king Shammar Yahri'sh takes Marib and ends the old kingdom of Saba, and soon rules all of southern Arabia.

title: Christians of Najran killed
description: The Jewish king Dhu Nuwas kills the Christians of Najran, which brings an Aksumite invasion from Ethiopia.

title: Persian conquest
description: A Sasanian force sent to help the Himyarite prince Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan drives out the Aksumites, and Yemen becomes a Persian province.

title: Persian governor accepts Islam
description: Badhan, the Sasanian governor, converts to Islam, and the new religion spreads through Yemen in the lifetime of Muhammad.

title: Zabid founded
description: Ibn Ziyad, sent by the Abbasid caliph, founds a city on the coastal plain that becomes the capital of his dynasty and a centre of Islamic learning.

title: Zaydi imamate founded
description: Al-Hadi ila'l-Haqq Yahya is invited to settle tribal disputes in the northern highlands and founds a line of Zaydi imams that lasts until 1962.

title: Queen Arwa moves the capital to Jibla
description: Arwa al-Sulayhi, who ruled Yemen in her own name for half a century, moves her court from Sanaa to Jibla.

title: Ayyubid conquest
description: Turan-Shah, brother of Saladin, takes Zabid, Aden and Sanaa and brings most of Yemen under one rule.

title: Rasulid dynasty founded
description: The Ayyubid deputy Umar ibn Ali makes himself independent, founding a dynasty that rules Yemen from Zabid and Taiz for more than two centuries.

title: Portuguese attack Aden
description: Afonso de Albuquerque fails to take the port that controls the entrance to the Red Sea.

title: Ottomans take Aden
description: An Ottoman fleet on its way to India seizes Aden, the start of Ottoman rule on the coasts of Yemen.

title: Ottomans driven out
description: The Zaydi imam al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad forces the last Ottoman troops to leave, and the imams rule a Yemen that grows rich on the coffee trade of Mocha.

title: British capture Aden
description: Troops of the East India Company take the port, which becomes a coaling station on the route to India and stays British until 1967.

title: Ottomans take Sanaa
description: Ottoman forces return to the highlands and make Sanaa the capital of a province, which they hold against repeated revolts until 1918.

title: Treaty of Daan
description: The Ottomans grant Imam Yahya authority over the Zaydi highlands after years of rebellion.

title: North Yemen becomes independent
description: With the defeat of the Ottoman Empire, Imam Yahya takes control of Sanaa and rules the north as an independent kingdom.

title: Treaty of Taif
description: After a short war won by Saudi Arabia, Yemen gives up its claims to Asir, Najran and Jizan.

title: Assassination of Imam Yahya
description: The imam is shot in an attempted coup, which his son Ahmad defeats within weeks.

title: Revolution in the north
description: Army officers overthrow the new imam and proclaim the Yemen Arab Republic, starting a civil war in which Egypt backs the republic and Saudi Arabia the royalists.

title: South Yemen becomes independent
description: Britain leaves Aden after four years of armed revolt and hands power to the National Liberation Front, which founds the only Marxist state in the Arab world.

title: Civil war in South Yemen
description: A shooting at a meeting of the ruling party's leadership starts eleven days of fighting between its factions that kills thousands.

title: Unification
description: North and South Yemen merge into the Republic of Yemen with Ali Abdullah Saleh as president and Sanaa as capital.

title: Northern forces take Aden
description: The fall of Aden ends a two-month civil war in which southern leaders tried to restore a separate state.

title: Bombing of USS Cole
description: Al-Qaeda suicide bombers in a small boat blow a hole in an American destroyer refuelling at Aden, killing 17 sailors.

title: Houthi insurgency begins
description: The government's attempt to arrest the Zaydi cleric Hussein al-Houthi starts the first of a series of wars in the northern mountains.

title: Uprising against Saleh
description: Large protests begin in Sanaa and continue until President Ali Abdullah Saleh agrees in November to hand over power after thirty-three years.

title: Houthis take Sanaa
description: Houthi fighters seize the capital and later remove the government, the start of the civil war.

title: Killing of Ali Abdullah Saleh
description: Houthi fighters kill the former president days after he broke his alliance with them.
